memory_update.text: BWXT should remain the reference anchor for US-listed advanced nuclear fuel fabrication and qualified nuclear components, but its market cap and attention level make it less attractive for the underfollowed lane.
Mirion is a stronger underfollowed mid-cap candidate for advanced nuclear instrumentation, radiation monitoring, dosimetry, and compliance infrastructure than reactor developers themselves.
CPSH belongs only in the speculative shadow list until nuclear shielding work is tied to named customers, material orders, DOE Phase II/III progress, or qualified manufacturing validation.

The most investable US-listed direct exposures for this node appear split between qualified component/fuel leaders, diversified nuclear component suppliers, instrumentation/compliance platforms, and very small advanced-materials suppliers.

summary: Layer 1B expansion for this node points to a two-lane universe: BWX Technologies as the best public reference anchor for nuclear components and TRISO fuel fabrication; Curtiss-Wright as a large, direct nuclear component and services supplier; Mirion as an underfollowed instrumentation, radiation monitoring, and advanced-reactor compliance platform; and CPS Technologies as a micro-cap speculative shadow tied to advanced composite radiation shielding for microreactors/SMRs. The chokepoint logic remains strongest where qualification, nuclear QA, licensing, and installed-fleet trust create long-cycle barriers. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation.
